original_question: Let A and B be the generators of two communicating C0 -semigroups on a Banach space and let G be the generator of the corresponding product semigroup. Find (the most general) conditions implying D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the correct operators A, B, and G; the Banach-space setting; the assumption that the two C_0-semigroups communicate; and the exact desired conclusion D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).
missing_details: The ambient Banach space should be named explicitly, say X; the problem statement in the paper says only “on a Banach space.”
The semigroups themselves should be introduced explicitly, e.g. (T(t))_{t≥0} and (S(t))_{t≥0}, rather than referring only to their generators.
To make the question stand-alone, “communicating” should be spelled out as a commutation relation such as T(t)S(s) = S(s)T(t) for all s,t ≥ 0.
The product semigroup should be identified explicitly as the one-parameter family U(t) = T(t)S(t), with G its generator.
It should be made explicit that the point is to determine hypotheses under which the domain identity holds; the paper does not supply such hypotheses, because this is the open problem itself.
The paper does not add any broader equivalent reformulation nearby; the only additional context is the comment that solving this would yield abstract maximal regularity results.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space, and let (T(t))_{t≥0} and (S(t))_{t≥0} be two communicating C_0-semigroups on X, meaning that T(t)S(s) = S(s)T(t) for all s,t ≥ 0, with generators A and B, respectively. Let U(t) := T(t)S(t) for t ≥ 0, and let G be the generator of the corresponding product semigroup U = (U(t))_{t≥0}. Determine the most general conditions under which D(G) = D(A) ∩ D(B).
justification: This is exactly the paper’s Problem 6 in Section 1. The draft should not be broadened to neighboring generator-sum or perturbation questions: the paper isolates this domain-identification problem as a separate open problem and adds only the brief motivation that it yields abstract maximal regularity results. Since no theorem, proposition, or remark nearby gives a more formal equivalent version, the faithful refinement is simply to make explicit the Banach space X, the two semigroups, the meaning of “communicating,” and the product semigroup U(t)=T(t)S(t).
